speaker: gauge
text: This ship has a bump under its nose. I'll cut it off!

speaker: fitz
text:
Wait. That bump is on purpose.
A moving ship pushes up a wave at its front. Making that wave burns fuel.
The bump makes its own wave, which partly cancels that one.

speaker: gauge
text: So it works at any speed?

speaker: fitz
text:
No. It's tuned for a certain speed. Too slow, and it can add drag.
When some container ships slowed down, owners swapped in new bumps shaped for the slower speed.

speaker: gauge
text: Ooh, what else is built weird? Subscribe and let's find out.
